findings.title: Pause button will never render in list view because it requires rulerRule to be defined
findings.body: The pause menu item rendering condition on line 123 requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` to be true. When this component is used from the alert list view (the stated goal of this PR), `rulerRule` is undefined because ruler API calls have been removed. Even though `canPause` may be true via the `grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed` path, the additional guard `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` will always be false when `rulerRule` is undefined, so the pause button will never appear in the list view.

findings.title: Delete button will never render in list view because it requires rulerRule to be truthy
findings.body: The delete menu item on line 165 is guarded by `canDelete && rulerRule`. When coming from the alert list view (where ruler API calls have been removed), `rulerRule` will be undefined, so the delete button will never render even if the user has delete permissions determined via the `grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed` path. This makes the delete action inaccessible from the list view.

findings.title: Silence drawer will not open when rulerRule is undefined (list view scenario)
findings.body: The SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is conditionally rendered with `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. When `rule` (the RulerRuleDTO) is undefined—which is the case in the list view where ruler calls are removed—clicking 'Silence notifications' in the menu will set `showSilenceDrawer` to true but the drawer will never render because the type guard fails. The user clicks the button and nothing visible happens.

findings.title: Extra closing brace in template literal produces incorrect key
findings.body: The function `getGrafanaRuleKey` returns `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}}` — note the trailing double `}}`. The extra closing brace becomes part of the key string, producing keys like `grafana-abc-group1-uid1}` instead of `grafana-abc-group1-uid1`. While this won't cause a crash, it produces incorrect key values and could cause issues if these keys are used for deduplication or comparison elsewhere.

findings.title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in list rendering
findings.body: In the `rules.map()` callback, the `key` variable is destructured from `ruleWithOrigin` on line 152, but it is not passed as a `key` prop to `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` on line 157. The `DataSourceRuleLoader` on line 165 correctly receives `key={key}`, but the Grafana case does not. React will fall back to using index-based reconciliation, which can cause rendering bugs when the list order changes or items are added/removed.

findings.title: Federated rule group check removed, causing regression for Mimir federated rules
findings.body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `isFederated` is now hardcoded to `false` with a TODO comment. Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (which now delegates to this function) checked `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. This means federated rule groups in Mimir/Cloud data sources will no longer be treated as immutable—users may see Edit/Delete buttons for federated rules that should be protected. The `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` type doesn't carry federation information, so this data is lost in the refactoring.

findings.title: Leftover development comment '// duplicate' in production code
findings.body: Line 289 has a trailing comment `// duplicate` on the `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` call that appears to be a leftover development note. It should be removed before merging.
